title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment measuring the operational effect of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipeline for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced one shared initial candidate reused across baseline and guarded conditions. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (operationalized as difference in success rates per preregistration). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); contingency cells n_11=199, n_10=1, n_01=0, n_00=0. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in actionable errors under the original power assumption) is not supported because the observed baseline actionable-error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed in power planning. All principal artifacts, provider-call accounting, validator traces, per-episode scoring JSONs, and analysis outputs are archived with SHA-256 digests for forensic verification.

sections.introduction: LLM-based generators promise faster intent→configuration translation for NetOps, but incorrect outputs can cause outages or policy violations. A common operational safeguard is to place a deterministic validator between generation and deployment and to enable automated repairs where possible. Prior LLM→NetOps evaluations typically report one-condition accuracies or leaderboard-style numbers without preregistration or forensic artifact tracing. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? We adopted a paired design to control task heterogeneity: for each task the initial LLM candidate was shared across conditions (shared_initial) and compared to the final guarded artifact (after deterministic validation and up to one automated repair). Key contribution: a fully preregistered, artifact-hashed, paired confirmatory run with deterministic validator traces and complete provider-call accounting enabling forensic reproducibility.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification and incremental checkers (header-space analysis, VeriFlow, etc.) are established pre-deployment safety tools. Recent LLM→NetOps research explores intent-driven config generation and programmatic repair, but often lacks preregistration, deterministic validators, or archived per-episode traces. NetConfEval and similar evaluations quantify model correctness but rarely isolate the marginal effect of an explicit deterministic guard applied to a fixed initial candidate. Our work differs by (1) enforcing shared_initial generation (same candidate for baseline and guarded paths), (2) using a deterministic validator that emits canonical ASTs and simulator-backed semantic checks (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), (3) bounding automated repair attempts (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1), and (4) publishing cryptographic hashes for primary artifacts so auditors can reproduce contingency tables and per-episode validator traces.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The preregistered design is paired binary (N=200). Primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = non-actionable, i.e., valid configuration per deterministic validator). Confirmatory test: exact two-sided McNemar on paired binary outcomes; supplementary paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (resamples = 10,000, seed = 1729). Planned stratification (preregistered) across vendor families: Cisco-like N=66, Juniper-like N=67, RFC-neutral N=67 (sampling templates archived). The preregistration contains sampling, missingness, retry, and multiplicity plans (SHA-256 above).

Adapter, model, and execution semantics. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false) so each task yielded one initial candidate reused for baseline and guarded conditions. The adapter allowed ≤1 automated repair per task; provider-call accounting is recorded in deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...). Execution manifest: planned_episode_count = 400 (200 pairs × 2 conditions), completed_episode_count = 400, model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair) and failed_episode_count = 0 (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...). All provider calls and stage counts are logged and hashed.

Task bank, validator, and scoring. Tasks were generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (synthetic multi-vendor templates). Each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, workflow policies (must_be_down_for_fields, group constraints), permitted fields, and required_sequence. The deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 parses responses to canonical ASTs, applies vendor-specific parse rules, enforces intent-constraints and workflow dependencies, and runs simulator-backed semantic checks. The validator returns validator_trace (validation_before, validation_after), a normalized_configuration string, violation codes, and a binary score (scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation). Per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ are the authoritative traces; representative examples and SHA-256 digests are archived in the evidence bundle.

Analysis and reproducibility. Analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 consuming execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...) and producing paired contingency counts, exact McNemar p-value, and paired bootstrap CI. Analysis artifacts and CSVs are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba..., analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 86ab6b56..., analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256 = dbc0bd6b...). All cryptographic digests in the Disclosure Statement are authoritative and sufficient for auditors to reconstruct every reported quantity.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline_success_count = 199 (success_rate = 0.995); guarded_success_count = 200 (success_rate = 1.000). Contingency-cell counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0): n_11 = 199 (guarded=1 & baseline=1), n_10 = 1 (guarded=1 & baseline=0; a guarded-only improvement), n_01 = 0 (guarded=0 & baseline=1), n_00 = 0 (both invalid). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI for the absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729).

Estimand algebra and interpretation. The preregistration targeted a ≥50% relative reduction in actionable-error rate; actionable_error_rate = 1 − success_rate. Observed baseline actionable-error rate = 1 − 0.995 = 0.005 (1/200). A 50% relative reduction of baseline error mass corresponds to an absolute reduction of 0.0025, which is smaller than the absolute effect scale assumed in the preregistered power calculation (the preregistration targeted an absolute reduction ≈0.15 for power ≈0.8 at N=200). Thus the preregistered confirmatory power assumption and the observed rare-failure regime are mismatched. Although the guarded pipeline produced the single discordant improvement (n_10 = 1) and eliminated the lone actionable error in this run, the observed effect is too small in absolute terms relative to the original power design to declare the preregistered confirmatory hypothesis supported.

Provider-call and repair accounting. Provider_call_audit (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...) reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 201. Stage counts: shared_initial_generation = 200, repair = 1, which aligns with model_calls_used = 201 recorded in the execution manifest (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...). The single repair call corresponds to the discordant episode record archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl and the per-episode scoring JSON under execution/scoring/; auditors can retrieve the explicit episode id and full validator_trace using those archived files and SHA-256 digests.
sections.discussion:
Operational significance and rarity regimes. In this bounded experimental regime—single model (gpt-5-mini), synthetic 200-task bank, deterministic validator v5, and at most one automated repair—the guarded pipeline reduced actionable errors in absolute terms from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute change = 0.005). When baseline error prevalence is this low, the marginal absolute benefit of a validator can be numerically tiny even when qualitatively important (an eliminated outage). System designers must therefore calibrate validation investments to expected baseline error prevalence, the cost of residual failures, and validator coverage. For example, when failure costs are high, even rare-event elimination may justify heavy validation; conversely, when baseline errors are rare and repair costs high, investment returns diminish.

Power, design lessons, and post-hoc sensitivity. The preregistered power calculation assumed substantially higher baseline error prevalence; the observed baseline of 1/200 implies that the trial as designed was underpowered to detect small relative reductions as confirmatory effects. Practical design adjustments for future confirmatory studies: (1) increase N to capture rare-event mass, (2) oversample higher-difficulty task strata where baseline errors cluster, or (3) adopt cost-weighted estimands that reflect operational loss from each failure type rather than raw proportion differences. Our artifacts and logs permit post-hoc sample-size sensitivity calculations and stratified reweighting by task difficulty, but we do not invent such post-hoc numeric power results in this manuscript beyond the qualitative conclusion that the original design's absolute-effect target was mismatched to observed rarity.

Reviewer-requested per-vendor stratification and discordant-episode identification. Reviewers asked for (i) verbatim per-vendor observed counts (Cisco-like / Juniper-like / RFC-neutral) and (ii) the explicit discordant episode identifier for the single baseline-invalid → guarded-valid pair. These exact observed values are deterministically computable from the archived execution artifacts: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) together with execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02) and the per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (full hash manifest listed in execution/execution_manifest.json). Because the supplied manuscript evidence bundle does not contain those verbatim derived numbers inlined, we provide artifact pointers and SHA-256 digests here so auditors can retrieve the exact per-vendor observed counts and the explicit episode id and validator_trace without ambiguity. If reviewers require the numeric table and identifier reproduced verbatim in the paper body, we will include them only after deterministic verification from the archived JSONs (we avoid inventing inline numerics that are not present verbatim in the supplied artifact content). This preserves forensic integrity and deterministic traceability.

Failure-mode diagnostics. The single baseline failure logged by the validator was classified by the per-episode validator_trace as a syntactic/ordering omission that the repair path corrected; analysis/contamination_summary.csv (SHA-256 = 389227f0...) records no systematic contamination clusters. Because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered secondary confirmatory test comparing residual error-type proportions (H2) could not be executed; any statements about residual error-type prevalence are therefore exploratory and limited by zero guarded failures. All per-episode validator_trace objects (validation_before, validation_after) are archived for auditing and post-hoc failure-mode clustering.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory run evaluating a deterministic-validator guard on a 200-task synthetic NetOps bank with gpt-5-mini. The guarded pipeline eliminated the single actionable error observed in baseline (199→200 successes), producing an absolute paired change of 0.005 (CI [0.0, 0.015]) but failing to satisfy the preregistered large-absolute-effect confirmatory target because the observed baseline error prevalence was far lower than assumed in power planning. We publish cryptographic hashes and authoritative artifact paths for all principal inputs, per-episode traces, provider-call accounting, and analysis outputs to enable deterministic re-computation of per-vendor stratifications, the discordant episode id, and every reported statistic. Future confirmatory work should expand model breadth, validator diversity, repair budgets, and task realism to identify regimes where deterministic validators yield large absolute operational risk reductions.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Reviewer-required per-vendor stratified observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are not included verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle; auditors can compute them from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02) but we do not invent those numeric summaries or identifiers in the manuscript where they are not present verbatim in the supplied archive.
